items.title: Bersatu calls out PN and Pas, saying 'don't play the victim'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has hit back at Perikatan Nasional and Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, saying "cowards" better describes PN leaders who avoid facing member parties. Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said PN leaders should not "play the victim". He said the term "cowards" could also be applied to those who abused administrative power and breached the PN constitution to deny Bersatu the right to attend the PN seat consultation committee meeting and the PN supreme council's extraordinary meeting.

items.title: More than 200 attend funeral of Gerik crash victim
items.summary: BACHOK: More than 200 family members, villagers and friends attended the funeral of one of the victims of a three-vehicle crash in Gerik, Perak, tonight. Mohamad Hafiz Daniel Nik Hairey, 19, was buried at 10.45pm at the Kampung Tok Jawa Islamic Cemetery in Budi here. His father, Nik Hairey Nik Rahim, 42, said the last time he saw his son was on Saturday night, before Hafiz left for Gerik at 4am on Sunday.

items.title: Thai youths carry on fight for right to dissent
items.summary: FIFTY years after a student demonstration against dictatorship ended in a massacre, Thailand's latest generation of protesters say they still face threats. Nutthanit Duangmusit, 24, spent several months in pre-trial detention before being convicted under Thailand's strict royal defamation law, among almost 300 people charged under so-called lese majeste since 2020. In one of the darkest chapters in modern Thai history, security forces and right-wing mobs massacred student protesters at one of the nation's top universities.

items.title: Repatriation of Myanmar detainees carried out in orderly, responsible and lawful manner - Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Any action regarding the repatriation of Myanmar detainees to their home country will be carried out in an orderly, responsible, and lawful manner, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the matter was among matters discussed during his meeting with the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) today to exchange views and obtain feedback regarding detainee management issues. "Among the matters discussed included the repatriation of Myanmar refugees to their home country, including implementation procedures and security aspects, in addition to humanitarian matters that Suhakam requested be given attention.

items.title: Trump won't be a quiet lame duck after midterm polls
items.summary: WHAT'S more volatile than President Donald Trump? The answer may be a lame duck Donald Trump after the United States midterm elections. "They'll probably go after me, and I'll go after them," Trump said in a Time Magazine interview published this week.

items.title: New legal certification course expected to begin by 2029 latest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The New Bar Course (NBC), which will replace the Certificate in Legal Practice (CLP) examination, is expected to be implemented in 2028, or, at the latest by 2029. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Sri Azalina Othman Said said the Legal Profession Qualifying Board had established a task force on April 27 to develop the operational framework for the new course. Azalina said preparations include developing course content and question banks for the Conversion Course (CC) and Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate (LPPC), as well as procuring learning management and computer-based assessment systems.

items.title: PTPTN loan arrears hit RM10.7bil involving 1.16mil borrowers
items.summary: PTPTN loan arrears hit RM10.7bil involving 1.16mil borrowers Amalia Azmi, Hakim Mahari KUALA LUMPUR: National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan arrears involving 1.16 million borrowers have reached RM10.7 billion as of Aug 31. The Higher Education Ministry said PTPTN was taking various measures to ensure the long-term sustainability of its financing model, including strengthening loan management and improving repayment collection. It said loan terms and conditions would be refined to better target financing to those in need, based on PTPTN's financial capacity.

items.title: Nearly 10,000 development projects worth RM944bil proposed for 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Economy Ministry has received 9,955 new and ongoing development project proposals costing RM944 billion for 2027. The ministry said a RM80.4 billion development ceiling would be required for consideration under the 2027 development planning process. "Under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) 2026-2030, ministries and agencies may submit applications for proposed development programmes and projects for consideration by the Economy Ministry through the rolling plan process," it said in a written parliamentary reply today.

items.title: NST Leader: Schools need stronger safeguards against violence
items.summary: It is ironic that while schools and hostels are meant to protect students, some of the gravest dangers can come from within. The Education Ministry's Student Discipline System recorded 21,307 bullying cases between 2021 and 2025. But repeated cases of violence raise a more fundamental question: are existing safeguards enough to protect students from threats within the school community?

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Monday, Oct 5, 2026
items.summary: Missed what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1548470]] [[nid:1548469]] [[nid:1548468]] [[nid:1548467]] [[nid:1548466]] [[nid:1548465]] [[nid:1548464]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 14 companies approved to rehabilitate 7,500ha of abandoned rubber estates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Rubber Board has approved the participation of 14 estate management companies (EMCs) under the Consolidation Programme for Abandoned and Untapped Mature Rubber Areas as of September. The Plantation and Commodities Ministry said this involved 7,576ha of abandoned rubber estates. The programme targets the rehabilitation of 3,000ha of abandoned and untapped mature rubber areas by 2027, aimed at bringing the land back into production and increasing national rubber output.

items.title: MCBA seizes 637 tonnes of cocoa beans worth RM11.9mil at Johor port
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) seized 637 tonnes of cocoa beans worth nearly RM11.9 million smuggled into the country in a container at Pasir Gudang Port, Johor, on Saturday. The agency, in a statement, said the beans were detected during an inspection by its enforcement officers about 3.50pm. It said the beans were in 9,100 gunny sacks and had been brought in from Uganda.

items.title: Dozens quarantined in Siberia after plague institute lab worker dies
items.summary: MOSCOW: A laboratory worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has fallen ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people, and the head of Russia's health watchdog to fly to the Irkutsk region. The death has sparked public health fears on social media, but the authorities said on Monday the situation was under control. Local media named the woman as Darya Shipilova, an employee at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East.

items.title: Father of girl, 3, killed in Gerik crash hadn't seen her in a year
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Mohamad Sanuzi Mohd Nawi had not seen his daughter in a year after divorcing her mother. Then came the sad news that the 3-year-old was one of four killed in a three-vehicle road crash on the East-West Highway yesterday. Safiyya Haura was killed along with her mother, Tuan Shazrin Tuan Mud, 40, and two other people in a crash at Km38.5 of the highway near Tasik Banding, Gerik, Perak, yesterday afternoon.

items.title: Police to submit MCBA DG investigation paper to A-G tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The investigation papers on the incident involving Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will be handed over to the Attorney-General's Chambers tomorrow. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the investigation papers would be referred for further review, advice and instructions, in accordance with Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution. "So far, statements have been recorded from 25 witnesses, comprising police officers and personnel, MCBA officers, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) auxiliary policemen, baggage handling system workers, medical officers and independent witnesses," he said in a statement.

items.title: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah visits Tun M at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah visited former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad at the National Heart Institute (IJN) here yesterday. The visit was shared on Dr Mahathir's official Facebook page, which said the Brunei ruler had visited the 101-year-old former prime minister at IJN on Oct 4. Dr Mahathir was admitted to IJN on Sept 29 for observation, a day after his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, died at the same hospital at the age of 100.

items.title: Ministry takes RON95 samples from 11 petrols stations over water-mixing claims
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: The Kedah Ministry of Domestic Trade and Costs of Living has taken RON95 petrol samples from 11 petrol stations in several districts for analysis following recent viral claims that the fuel was mixed with water. State director Muhammad Nizam Jamaludin said the action followed public complaints that vehicles had broken down after refuelling at the affected stations. "Ministry enforcement teams conducted inspections at 11 petrol stations today and took fuel samples from the involved tanks or pumps for inspection and further analysis.

items.title: Zetrix AI offers plan to settle RM314mil RTD arrears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has submitted a proposal to the government to resolve outstanding remittances following the suspension of its Road Transport Department (RTD) services from today. In its statement today, Zetrix AI said its immediate priority is to resolve the outstanding obligations and work towards restoring the affected services, subject to necessary government approvals. "Zetrix AI has submitted a proposed solution to the government of Malaysia to address the outstanding remittances for its consideration," it said.

items.title: AG's Report: Govt accounts receivable down 1.1 per cent to RM102bil in 2025
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Government's Accounts Receivable (AR) fell by 1.1 per cent to RM102.032 billion in 2025 from RM103.158 billion the previous year, according to the Auditor General's Report 2/2026. The report stated that the RM1.126 billion decrease was partly due to the write-off of revenue AR and loan interests amounting to RM1.207 billion, as well as RM603 million in guarantee fees no longer reported as AR. The report also confirmed that total outstanding AR for utility relocation costs amounted to RM90.50 million.

items.title: Universities are not only path to youth success - Zambry Abd Kadir
items.summary: He said knowledge and skills in technical fields also opened up career opportunities for young people, including those who were less academically inclined. He said this during the "Technology Driving Change: Is Malaysian Talent Ready?" Zambry said teaching approaches at skills institutions were also being strengthened to meet the country's demand for technical workers, including the government's effort to produce 60,000 engineers.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 5, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: MYEG owes RM314m Transport Minister Anthony Loke says MYEG and Zetrix failed to remit RM314 million in government revenue since May. e-Jamin lacked contract The Public Accounts Committee says the e-Jamin bail system operated for five years without a formal government contract. F1 return to Sepang Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says Sultan Ibrahim's ties with Bahrain's king helped pave the way for F1's return to Malaysia.

items.title: Yemeni government forces seize district by Bab el-Mandeb, military sources say
items.summary: RIYADH: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces seized key positions on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Monday, military and government sources said, as they fought to reverse last month's advances by the Iran-backed Houthis and drive them from the vital waterway. The government forces have taken large parts of Dhubab district, which overlooks Bab el-Mandeb, and are asserting full control over the area with heavy air support from a Saudi-led coalition, three military sources and one government source told Reuters. Houthi-aligned media had earlier denied that government forces had made advances in the area.

items.title: Four issues Felda must resolve under new plan
items.summary: Zuraimi Abdullah KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Land Development Authority's (Felda) new strategic plan must address or redefine four fundamental issues if the agency is to achieve long-term financial sustainability. They are Felda's commercial mandate, fragmented settler land, non-core assets and legal framework. The White Paper concluded that weak financial management and governance shortcomings had adversely affected Felda's financial position.

items.title: Bersatu ready to discuss cooperation for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is ready to discuss and refine the form of cooperation or an electoral pact for the upcoming Melaka state election, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali. He said the matter was among the decisions reached at the Bersatu Political Bureau meeting chaired by its president, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, today. Mohamed Azmin said the decision was made after taking into account views and analyses on Bersatu's participation in the Melaka election, including various aspects of the current political landscape.

items.title: IGP: Police record statements from 25 witnesses in KLIA incident involving border agency chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Police have recorded statements from 25 witnesses as part of investigations into allegations that the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) physically assaulted two police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28. In a statement issued today, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said that the two officers had lodged police reports over the alleged incident. The 25 witnesses whose statements have been recorded include PDRM officers and personnel, AKPS officers, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) auxiliary police personnel, baggage-handling system workers, medical officers and independent witnesses.

items.title: 6m-tall tree falls across road in Batu Ferringhi
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call at 4.27pm regarding the incident in front of the Spice Garden along Jalan Teluk Bahang. "Firefighters from the Teluk Bahang station found a tree had fallen across the road when they arrived," he said. John said three firefighters carried out cutting and clearing works to remove the obstruction.

items.title: Johor to aid MoE in strengthening school security measures after Yong Peng murder
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The Johor government is ready to review and assist with basic infrastructure needs in schools across the state to strengthen security measures, says Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi. Onn Hafiz voiced full support for any initiative implemented by the Education Ministry, particularly the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in strategic areas within the school grounds. Meanwhile, State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said discussions would be held soon between the state education department and the Batu Pahat district education office.

items.title: Higher education minister: Universities not only path to youth success
items.summary: He said knowledge and skills in technical fields also opened up career opportunities for young people, including those who were less academically inclined. He said this during the "Technology Driving Change: Is Malaysian Talent Ready?” He said technical and engineering fields did not necessarily depend solely on degree qualifications, but also required skilled workers who had undergone engineering-related training at skills institutions.

items.title: Go Hub unit bags RM64.79 mil deal in maintenance, support services for KTMB ticketing system
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Go Hub Capital Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary NSS IT Solution Sdn Bhd has accepted a letter of acceptance from Tenang Capital Bhd (TCB) for the provision of maintenance and support services for the Integrated Ticketing System of Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) worth RM64.79 million. TCB is a wholly owned subsidiary of KTMB. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Defence minister: LCS missile compensation claim expected to take time
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Recovering funds linked to the procurement of missiles for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) will not be resolved immediately and will take time, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. He said that although requests for Norway’s assistance had been made at various levels, including by the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), Foreign Minister (Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan) and himself, Norway had refused to intervene. Mohamed Khaled said the Norwegian government’s lack of intervention has left Malaysia to pursue its claim directly with the company, which he said has given various excuses.

items.title: Privasia Unit gets Miti nod for Bagan Datuk data centre project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Privasia Technology Bhd's indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, Silver Streams Technofarm Sdn Bhd (SSTF), has received approval from the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) to develop a data centre project in Bagan Datuk, Perak. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Privasia said MITI, via its letter dated Sept 7, 2026, approved SSTF's application for the development of the project. "The approval granted by MITI is subject to standard regulatory terms and conditions, which include the requirement to secure an off-grid energy supply with a maximum demand of 50 megawatts.

items.title: Citaglobal engineering unit secures RM29mil Thailand WTE supply contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd's subsidiary LAWI Engineering GmbH (LAWI Germany) has secured an engineering and equipment supply contract worth approximately RM29 million for the Siam Power Naklang waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Thailand. Citaglobal said the contract covers the engineering, procurement and construction of the project's steam boiler plant, as well as basic engineering for the technology component of the overall WTE power plant. LAWI Germany will undertake the imported engineering and equipment supply scope valued at approximately RM29 million, or EUR6.33 million, while its consortium partner will undertake the local scope valued at approximately RM23.1 million, or THB189.6 million.

items.title: Tech advances, including AI, gig economy, need workforce planning and regulation - Fahmi
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that if technological developments are allowed to run too freely without any regulation, it risks affecting workers' welfare and damaging the existing business ecosystem. in conjunction with the Launching of the Communications and Multimedia Future Skills Framework (C&M FSF) and Strategic Talent Development Initiative at Angkasapuri here today. Also present as dialogue panelists were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and Deputy Minister of Human Resources Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akhbar Khan.

items.title: IGP: Don’t hide school safety issues to protect reputations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Safety issues in schools should not be concealed to protect reputations, as this may prevent authorities from taking action, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail. Mohd Khalid said school safety is a shared responsibility requiring cooperation among PDRM, schools, the Ministry of Education, and parents. School liaison officers also regularly visit and coordinate with school authorities on safety issues.

items.title: Johor MB: State government ready to help schools review security measures following student’s death
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — The Johor state government is ready to review and assist with basic infrastructure needs in schools across the state to strengthen security measures, says Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi. Onn Hafiz expressed full support for any initiative implemented by the Education Ministry (MOE), particularly the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in strategic areas within school premises. Meanwhile, State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said discussions would be held soon between the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) and the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD).

items.title: PM Anwar: Land encroachment must be taken seriously
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Good governance practices must continue to be upheld, while any form of unauthorised land encroachment must not be taken lightly as it could affect national planning and the interests of the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he stressed these points while chairing the 83rd National Land Council meeting. “Land management must be carried out prudently and systematically to minimise risks to environmental sustainability,” he said.

items.title: Warehouse worker pleads not guilty to driving under the influence, injuring two marathon runners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 —An e-commerce platform warehouse worker pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of riding a motorcycle under the influence of alcohol, causing injuries to two participants of a running event last Saturday. Lawyer Muhammad Iqbal Azmi from the National Legal Aid Foundation, representing Muhammad Saiful, appealed for a bail reduction, saying that his client was single and earned RM1,500 a month. Magistrate Aliaa Anwar granted Muhammad Saiful bail of RM500 with one surety for each charge and set Jan 7, 2027, for case mention and submission of documents.

items.title: Govt launches framework to prepare communications, multimedia workforce for AI-driven changes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The federal government today launched a new framework to align communications and multimedia industry needs with education and skills development as artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, emerging technologies and the green economy reshape the sector. Its implementation will also involve the Higher Education and Human Resources ministries to align industry needs with education and skills development. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the framework identifies industry needs while aligning government, industry and education efforts to keep talent development in step with technological and economic changes.

items.title: ‘Touch ‘n Go rep’ scam leaves Kedah woman RM150 poorer, says consumer group
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 5 — A 39-year-old self-employed woman lost about RM150, including her BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) petrol subsidy and reward points, after a phone scammer posing as a Touch ‘n Go representative compromised her e-wallet. Kedah Consumers Association (Cake) president Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff said the victim lodged a report at the association’s office yesterday. “The victim said the caller offered her a new Touch ‘n Go card with various perks, including reward points, store vouchers offering discounts of up to 80 per cent, and overseas spending capabilities.

items.title: Penang stays on alert for human rabies after Kedah man dies of infection
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 5 — Penang has recorded no human rabies cases since the last two cases were reported in 1975, with the Penang State Health Department remaining on standby to respond to any possible cases. State Youth, Sports and Health Committee chairman Daniel Gooi Zi Sen said no animal rabies cases had also been detected in the state to date. Gooi said the state government was also working with the Department of Veterinary Services to monitor the rabies situation in Penang.

items.title: High Court rejects Bar bid to challenge Ahmad Terrirudin’s JAC appointment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The High Court today dismissed the Malaysian Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings challenging the appointment of Federal Court judge Ahmad Terrirudin Salleh to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC), according to a report by Free Malaysia Today (FMT). Justice Norliza Othman, in delivering her decision, held that Section 5(1)(e) of the JAC Act 2009 was unambiguous. Terrirudin, a former attorney-general, was elevated to the Federal Court in November 2024.

items.title: Woman, 69, found dead in parked car after discharge from Melaka Hospital
items.summary: Melaka Tengah district police chief ACP Halim Abas said in a statement today that the woman was found at about 4pm after she was discharged from Melaka Hospital, still wearing hospital clothes with her left arm in a sling. Her 44-year-old son received a call from Melaka Hospital at 1.50pm to take her home. She was wearing hospital clothes as she had no spare clothes,” he said.

items.title: Electric buses hit the test track as Rapid Penang gears up for greener rides
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 5 — Rapid Penang will conduct test runs of two electric buses on Oct 6 and 7, marking an initial step towards the introduction of electric buses into Penang’s public transport system. In a statement today, Rapid Penang said the initiative was part of Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd’s ongoing efforts to replace existing buses with safer, more sustainable and environmentally friendly vehicles, while enhancing operational efficiency. “The test run involves two electric buses from different manufacturers, namely a 12-metre Foton bus and an 8.25-metre Golden Dragon bus.

items.title: PAS MP calls for humane approach to Rohingya refugees amid calls for tighter controls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — PAS lawmaker Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman today called on the government to strike a balance in managing Rohingya refugees, saying a strict immigration policy must also be humane. “We must protect national security, control our borders, and maintain strong registration systems, but in doing so, we cannot lose our humanity and sense of justice,” Sik MP Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman said when addressing the House during a debate on refugee management. Such a system, he said, would properly distinguish genuine refugees from economic migrants, undocumented immigrants and victims of human trafficking.

items.title: Malaysia’s statutory debt at RM1.295t, or 63.9pc of GDP, still within legal limit, says Auditor General’s report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The Federal Government’s statutory debt-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio stood at 63.9 per cent last year, remaining below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, according to the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026. According to the report, the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills. “This ratio remains below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, as stipulated under the Loans (Local) (Statutory Limit on Borrowing) and Government Funding (Statutory Limit on Moneys Received) Order 2022,” it said.

items.title: Chicken curry, evening drives and a white cat: Song Swee Guan’s family remembers the man behind the Sarawak politician
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 5 — Sarawakian statesman Datuk Song Swee Guan has been remembered as a selfless and caring man who was able to balance between work and family. According to Song’s niece Kaylene Tan, his dedication to his work and selfless care for his parents kept him single. Sarawakian statesman Datuk Song Swee Guan was known to be a good cook by family members.

items.title: Planes, not just ships: Myanmar says most migrants returned from Malaysia flew home, as UN criticises Putrajaya’s scheme
items.summary: YANGON, Oct 5 — Myanmar has repatriated nearly 10,000 migrants from Malaysia this year, state media said on Monday, a day after a flotilla returning almost 1,500 of its citizens docked in the country. The United Nations (UN) has sharply criticised Malaysia’s push to return migrants to Myanmar under an opaque scheme it says cannot guarantee safe homecomings to the war-torn nation. A group of 1,476 returnees arrived by ship outside Yangon on Sunday, the first of 5,000 that Kuala Lumpur says Myanmar agreed to take back amid a wave of anti-migrant sentiment in Malaysia.

items.title: Targeted subsidy reforms help cut Malaysia’s 2025 bill by RM15.67b, federal audit shows
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The government has managed to reduce its subsidy expenditure by 40.1 per cent to RM23.43 billion in 2025 from RM39.10 billion in 2024, supported by the decline in crude oil prices and the implementation of the targeted diesel and petrol subsidy reforms. Petrol subsidy expenditure fell 46.5 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) to RM10.51 billion from RM19.66 billion in 2024, while diesel subsidy expenditure declined 48.2 per cent y-o-y to RM5.98 billion from RM11.54 billion previously. Meanwhile, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) subsidy expenditure decreased 29.1 per cent y-o-y to RM2.63 billion from RM3.71 billion previously.

items.title: State audits flag governance weaknesses despite clean financial opinions
items.summary: The National Audit Department (JAN), in a statement regarding the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026 today, announced that these findings follow the completion of audits on all 13 State Government Financial Statements for the year ending Dec 31, 2025. JAN also issued Auditor General’s Certificates for 298 State Agencies for the 2024 financial year and reported the results of performance audits conducted on 22 State Government programmes and activities. LKAN 2/2026, covering the Federal Government Financial Statements for 2025, activities of Federal Government Ministries/Departments, State Government and State Agency Financial Statements, activities of State Ministries/Departments/Agencies, and the management of State Government-owned companies, was tabled in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Govt’s dividend income edges up 1.4pc to RM39.55b, with Petronas paying most of it, says A-G
items.summary: Based on the report, BNM’s dividend increased to RM5.25 billion in 2025 from RM2.85 billion in 2024, while Khazanah Nasional Bhd’s dividend increased to RM2 billion in 2025 from RM1 billion in 2024. The total dividends of statutory bodies increased by 81.8 per cent to RM5.275 billion from RM2.902 billion, while the total dividends of companies decreased by 5.1 per cent to RM34.271 billion from RM36.109 billion. “Overall, the dividend receipts from nine companies and one statutory body amounted to RM7.433 billion compared to RM3.982 billion in 2024, an increase of RM3.451 billion (86.7 per cent).

items.title: Prosecution to call up to 20 witnesses as GISBH money laundering trial proceeds at Shah Alam court
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — The Sessions Court here was informed today that the representation submitted by the former chief executive officer (CEO) of GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and three former company accountants to drop money laundering charges against them had been rejected. Following this, Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Ashrof Adrin, who appeared alongside DPP Muhamad Ehsan Nasarudin, said the prosecution would proceed with the trial. The four accused are Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, 67, who faces 77 charges involving more than RM10 million; Hamimah Yakub, 74, facing 95 charges involving RM11.4 million; Asmat @ Asmanira Muhammad Ramly, 46, facing 68 charges involving RM4.7 million; and Mohd Khushairi Osman, 55, facing 91 charges involving nearly RM12 million.

items.title: Binning edible food a ‘grave sin’, says housing minister as nearly 16,000 tonnes tossed daily
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Nearly 40 per cent of the 40,000 metric tonnes of solid waste generated in the country daily consists of food waste, according to Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga said this when replying to a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) regarding the latest developments in efforts to reduce waste sent to landfills and increase recycling rates. Additionally, Nga said a school-based recycling competition involving 1,680 schools successfully collected 4.95 million kilogrammes of recyclable materials, which were sold for RM2.98 million.

items.title: No mandatory e-Consular registration yet, but foreign minister wants Malaysians abroad to sign up to make contact in emergencies easier
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The government does not yet intend to make registration on the e-Consular system mandatory for Malaysians abroad, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said registration through the digital platform managed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs remains voluntary, but Malaysians residing, travelling or studying abroad are highly encouraged to register to facilitate monitoring and welfare matters. “Not yet (making registration mandatory).

items.title: Record RM4.64b income, highest payout in eight years: Zulkifli Hasan says Tabung Haji’s governance now stronger
items.summary: This development is reflected, among other things, in TH recording its highest investment income in history, he said. Zulkifli said TH has a systematic investment process, which includes assessing investment, risk and shariah aspects before making any investment decision. For the 2025 financial year, TH’s investment income rose to RM4.64 billion, the highest level recorded.

items.title: Police vow no cover-up in probe into schoolgirl’s death in Yong Peng
items.summary: Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigation would be conducted comprehensively and professionally, with no attempt to cover up the case or protect any party. Police said the school and Education Ministry were cooperating fully with the investigation. The case remains under investigation.

items.title: Yong Peng school had CCTV but none at the crime scene, security firm under probe, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The secondary school in Yong Peng, Johor, where a Form Four female student was allegedly found murdered, is equipped with CCTV cameras, but none were installed at the location where the incident occurred. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the Ministry of Education (MOE) is now upgrading the CCTV facilities and has launched an investigation into the school’s security company to determine whether there were any breaches of standard operating procedures (SOPs). Justice for Irene Sofiya,” she said.

items.title: RM68.81m in contractor advance payments still unrecovered, Audit Dept finds
items.summary: “RM59.63 million out of RM68.81 million in WPK receivables outstanding for more than 10 years involved 21 companies,” the report read. The report stated that five of the companies had been dissolved, involving WPK receivables amounting to RM10.68 million, while 13 companies had been wound up, involving outstanding WPK of RM27.76 million. Another three companies remained active, with outstanding WPK amounting to RM21.19 million.

items.title: Puspakom opens Kajang centre with capacity to inspect 800 vehicles daily
items.summary: KAJANG, Oct 5 — Puspakom Sdn Bhd today began operations at its new inspection centre in Bandar Teknologi Kajang, with the facility eventually able to handle up to 800 vehicles a day. Private vehicle inspections began today, while Routine and Re-Routine inspections for light commercial vehicles will be introduced on October 28, followed by Initial and Re-Initial inspections from November 23. Puspakom said the phased opening was aimed at ensuring operational readiness while providing customers with a smoother inspection experience.

items.title: Perikatan parties file judicial review challenging ROS suspension, show-cause letter
items.summary: PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the application for judicial review was filed by the secretary-generals of all PN component parties. Takiyuddin said the coalition wants the judicial review application to be expedited given that the Melaka state election is approaching. Coalition leaders said the ROS suspension could disrupt PN’s preparations for the Melaka state polls, with it still unclear whether the coalition can contest under its own banner.

items.title: ‘Who sent the threats?’ Businessman seeks answers from police a year after Caprice case classified NFA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Maritime industry executive Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan, who was investigated over alleged threats made against social media influencer Caprice and his family, wants to know whether anyone has since been identified as being behind the threats. The chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd said a year had passed since Caprice lodged the complaint against him, and it was important for him to know the outcome, particularly as he had been questioned by police for several hours before the case was classified as no further action (NFA). “I totally understand that the police investigated based on Caprice’s complaint.
